# How do I get in

Generated 2026-10-11 · 26 services with an address · `<domain>` is the platform's domain, `<env>` its environment.

## 1. The normal way

Sign in once at `authentik.<domain>` — your password and your second factor. Its start page lists the services your groups open.

A service is opened by a **group**, never by a personal account: to get in somewhere, ask for the group named in the table below. Nothing else has to be created for you.

## 2. A login you have to type

A few services keep a local administrator that single sign-on does not cover. Automation creates that login and keeps it in Vault — you read it there, it is copied nowhere else:

1. Open `vault.<domain>`, choose the sign-in method **OIDC**, sign in with the same account.
2. Your groups' logins are the paths of the last column below.
3. What was generated for you alone (your first password, your keys) is in your own area: `secret/<env>/users/<your username>/`.

You can read, not write. Every read is logged. Another person's area is refused — to the administrators of Vault too.

What you create yourself (an app password for a mail program, recovery codes) goes in your own password manager, `vaultwarden.<domain>` — not in Vault.

## 3. When single sign-on is down

Nobody reaches Vault through single sign-on then. Getting back in is the emergency kit (Vault's unseal keys, the emergency account, the `root` passwords), held by the platform owner off the platform.

## 4. If a name does not load

Three things must hold, in this order: your desk routes the platform's networks through the firewall (the VPN does it for you); the name resolves to the platform's entry point (the platform's resolver does it); your address is allowed for that class of service — the column **Reachable from**.
